arxiv-2303-07436.title: Operational realization of quantum vacuum ambiguities
arxiv-2303-07436.creator: Álvaro Álvarez-Domínguez, José A.R. Cembranos, Luis J. Garay, Mercedes Martín-Benito, Álvaro Parra-López, Jose M. Sánchez Velázquez
arxiv-2303-07436.description: Abstract We provide a reinterpretation of the quantum vacuum ambiguities that one encounters when studying particle creation phenomena due to an external and time-dependent agent. We propose a measurement-motivated understanding: Each way of measuring the number of created particles selects a particular vacuum.

arxiv-2306-12941.title: Towards Reliable Evaluation and Fast Training of Robust Semantic Segmentation Models
arxiv-2306-12941.creator: Francesco Croce ∗, Naman D. Singh ∗, Matthias Hein
arxiv-2306-12941.description: Abstract Adversarial robustness has been studied extensively in image classification, especially for the ℓ ∞ \ell_{\infty} -threat model, but significantly less so for related tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation, where attacks turn out to be a much harder optimization problem than for image classification. We propose several problem-specific novel attacks minimizing different metrics in accuracy and mIoU.

arxiv-2407-00434.title: Brevity is the soul of wit: Pruning long files for code generation
arxiv-2407-00434.creator:
ame Aaditya K. Singh \email aaditya.singh.21@ucl.ac.uk, 
ame Yu Yang \email yuyang@cs.ucla.edu, 
ame Kushal Tirumala \email ktirumala@meta.com, 
ame Mostafa Elhoushi \email m.elhoushi@ieee.org, 
ame Ari S. Morcos \email ari@datologyai.com
arxiv-2407-00434.description: Abstract Data curation is commonly considered a “secret-sauce” for LLM training, with higher quality data usually leading to better LLM performance. Given the scale of internet-scraped corpora, data pruning has become a larger and larger focus. Specifically, many have shown that de-duplicating data, or sub-selecting higher quality data, can lead to efficiency or performance improvements.

arxiv-2409-13043.title: Pattern Localisation in the Swift-Hohenberg Equation via Slowly Varying Spatial Heterogeneity Thanks:
arxiv-2409-13043.creator: Andrew L. Krause, Václav Klika, Edgardo Villar-Sepúlveda, Alan R. Champneys, Eamonn A. Gaffney
arxiv-2409-13043.description: Abstract Theories of localised pattern formation are important to understand a broad range of natural patterns, but are less well-understood than more established mechanisms of domain-filling pattern formation. Here, we extend recent work on pattern localisation via slow spatial heterogeneity in reaction-diffusion systems to the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

arxiv-2506-17445.title: Multi-NARP Laser Driving Scheme for Multiplexed Quantum Networks Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2506-17445.creator: Ali Binai motlagh, 1, † {\dagger} Grant Wilbur, 2, † {\dagger} Nour Allam, 2 Giannis Tolis, 2 Lilly Daw, 2 S. O’Neal, 3, ‡ \ddagger Dennis G. Deppe, 3, § \mathsection and Kimberley C. Hall 2,*
arxiv-2506-17445.description: Abstract We extend the recently developed NARP scheme for laser-triggered single-photon sources to the simultaneous excitation of multiple emitters with varying transition energies, laying the groundwork for wavelength-division multiplexing in quantum optical networks. Our Multi-NARP scheme does not rely on polarization filtering and thus enables the near-unity extraction efficiency of single photons from each quantum dot.

arxiv-2509-18560.creator: CLARITA HAWAT, WISSAM AL JURDI, JACQUES BOU ABDO, Jacques Demerjian, Abdallah Makhoul
arxiv-2509-18560.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by CLARITA HAWAT, WISSAM AL JURDI, JACQUES BOU ABDO, Jacques Demerjian, Abdallah Makhoul. The exponential growth of web content is a major key to the success for Recommender Systems. This paper addresses the challenge of defining noise, which is inherently related to variability in human preferences and behaviours. In classifying changes in user tendencies, we distinguish three kinds of phenomena: external factors that directly influence users’ sentiment, serendipity causing unexpected preference, and incidental interaction perceived as noise.

arxiv-2602-12360.title: Predicting Dynamic Map States from Limited Field-of-View Sensor Data
arxiv-2602-12360.creator: Knut Peterson, David Han
arxiv-2602-12360.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Knut Peterson, David Han. When autonomous systems are deployed in real-world scenarios, sensors are often subject to limited field-of-view (FOV) constraints, either naturally through system design, or through unexpected occlusions or sensor failures. In conditions where a large FOV is unavailable, it is important to be able to infer information about the environment and predict the state of nearby surroundings based on available data to maintain safe and accurate operation.

pmc-11338328.title: Abstract 27: Physiologic Oxygen Expansion Enhances Lymphocyte and Neutrophil Recovery Following Transplantation
pmc-11338328.creator: Sarah Gutch, Jim Ropa, Lindsay Beasley, Grace Whitacre, Wouter Van't Hof, Maegan Capitano
pmc-11338328.description: IntroductionExpeditious recovery of lymphocytes after hematopoietic cell transplantation is a major determinant of patient outcome. pmc-11592201.description: Diosgenin (DSG) is a phytosterol saponin mainly found in Dioscorea zingiberensis C.H. Wright. Diosgenin is also an important medicinal chemical for synthesizing various steroid medicines.

pmc-11620146.title: Deep learning neural network-assisted badminton movement recognition and physical fitness training optimization
pmc-11620146.creator: Chuanbao He, Min Zhang
pmc-11620146.description: This work aims to solve the problem of low accuracy in recognizing the trajectory of badminton movement. This work focuses on the visual system in badminton robots and conducts side detection and tracking of flying badminton in two-dimensional image plane video streams. Then, the cropped video images are input into a convolutional neural network frame by frame.

pmc-12510510.title: Effects of human development, primary care coverage and the COVID-19 pandemic on the fertility rate among adolescents in Brazil in the period 2012–2021
pmc-12510510.creator: Rosa Maria Soares Madeira Domingues, Rafael Sant´Ana Herzog, Marcos Augusto Bastos Dias, Rossana Pulcineli Vieira Francisco, Agatha Sacramento Rodrigues, Claudia Osorio-de-Castro, Claudia Osorio-de-Castro, Claudia Osorio-de-Castro
pmc-12510510.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The high fertility rate (FR) in adolescents is a global public health problem, with the Americas region having the second highest FR in the world. This study aims to carry out a temporal and spatial analysis of the FR in adolescents in Brazil in the period 2012−2021 and evaluate the effects of primary care population (PCP) coverage on the FR in adolescents in different contexts of human development, measured by the Municipal Human Development Index (HDI-M).

pmc-13156650.title: IBS stress reactivity phenotype is associated with blood transcriptome profiles and microstructural and functional brain changes
pmc-13156650.creator: Jennifer S Labus, Desiree R Delgadillo, Steve Cole, Chencai Wang, Swapna Joshi, Arpana Church, Bruce Naliboff, Lin Chang, Jonathan P Jacobs, Benjamin M Ellingson, Emeran A Mayer
pmc-13156650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Evidence suggests significant interindividual differences in stress reactivity (SR), but mechanisms and therapeutic implications of these differences are poorly understood. The aim of this study was to identify the biological basis of increased SR by investigating associations between a psychometric-based phenotype with blood transcriptomics profiles of unprovoked tonic increased sympathetic nervous system (SNS) activation and neuroimaging phenotypes in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) participants and healthy controls (HCs).
